style.vernacular: Humid subtropical riverside capital: low colonial and neo-colonial houses in whitewashed or pastel render with red clay-tile or corrugated roofs, shaded corredor galleries on timber posts and wrought-iron window grilles; mid-century neoclassical and Art Deco public buildings; concrete and brick mid-rise blocks and glass-fronted malls on the main avenues, with lapacho, mango and palm street trees.
style.ornament: Colonial corredor galleries on carved timber posts, adobe walls under red tile, wrought-iron rejas on windows, neoclassical pilasters and pediments from the Lopez era, Art Deco geometry in 1930s blocks, flowering lapacho trees and nanduti lace-pattern motifs.

sources.what: colonial wood and adobe giving way to masonry classicism under Carlos Antonio Lopez, later neo-colonial and Art Deco, Brazilian modernism, 1970s Itaipu-driven building boom
neighbouring-city houses described with colonial and neoclassical influence, tile roofs, brick walls and pastel colours
